extracted.intended_audience: public information officers (PIOs), emergency managers, government communicators, and prospective PIO trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and training guidance for Public Information Officers to plan, prepare, and execute public information activities before, during, and after incidents, emphasizing strategic community-wide communications and practical exercises. Focuses on skills progression from basic awareness to executive-level responsibilities and the 95/5 non‑emergency/emergency concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Right Message, to the Right People, at the Right Time
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Disaster & Emergency Management University (NDEMU) PIO training program is designed to provide PIOs with the essential knowledge, skills, and abilities to support proper decision-making by delivering the right message, to the right people, at the right time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the program's central objective and evaluative standard: communications should be appropriate (right message), targeted (right people), and timely (right time). Training, exercises, and course evaluations should measure performance against this triad.

rubrics_metrics.name: 95/5 Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The 95/5 concept: about 95% of PIO work is completed in non-emergency times, while typically about 5% is directly related to incident response or recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that non-emergency activities (planning, relationship-building, preparedness) substantially determine effectiveness during the small fraction of time spent in response/recovery. Training and assessment should cover both non-emergency preparedness and emergency execution, showing how routine tasks support crisis performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO Core Tasks: gather, verify, coordinate, and disseminate public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Public information entails the processes and systems that enable effective communications with various target audiences. The PIO program provides the opportunity to learn and practice the tasks of gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating public information at all levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance criteria should include accuracy (verification), timeliness (dissemination), collaboration (coordination), and information collection (gathering). Exercises and coursework should test each task across jurisdictional levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole Community Strategic Communications Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The courses in this series thematically focus on the 95/5 concept and whole community strategic communications planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should measure ability to plan communications that consider the entire community—multiple audiences, stakeholders, partners—and to integrate strategies that reach and serve diverse populations before, during, and after incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive Skill Development: awareness & basics to advanced and master levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO program series moves progressively through public information awareness & basics to advanced PIO concepts, and culminates in a master public information officer course series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum and assessments are tiered: foundational knowledge and basic skills for entry/part-time PIOs, advanced applied skills, then executive/master-level strategic competencies. Success criteria should match the expected skill level of each tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Awareness and Basics (course competency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlying concepts, and the basic skills needed for full or part time PIOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry-level competency includes understanding core concepts of public information operations and basic practical skills; course completion/assessment should verify these foundational abilities for both full- and part-time PIOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Public Information Officer (applied competency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply advanced public information skills in a multi-day functional exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced-level training requires applying skills in realistic, multi-day functional exercises that simulate incident conditions. Evaluation should focus on applied performance: message production, coordination, verification under stress, and multi-channel dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Public Information Officer (strategic/leadership competency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanded role in delivering strategic public information and warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive-level criteria include strategic leadership in public information and warning—developing and overseeing communications strategy, cross-agency coordination, and high-level decision support. Assessments should examine strategic planning, policy-level coordination, and oversight capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on non-emergency posture activities to improve emergency effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The activities a PIO engages in during a non-emergency posture (95%) has a significant impact on how successful they will be in the 5% spent in emergency response and recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and training should weight and measure non-emergency activities—relationship building, preparedness messaging, planning, and exercises—since these underpin effective crisis response. Success metrics may include established partnerships, pre-developed messaging, and tested plans.
